In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dosimetry of radiation in cell culture and in small and large animal studies should be performed with the highest standards of precision and accuracy, with the results reported with sufficient details to allow the work be interpreted, repeated, and compared to other laboratories.

the workshop participants agreed that the field would benefit greatly from the development of a set of dosimetry SOPs for radiobiology and that such SOPs should be widely distributed and made readily accessible to the research community.
there is a strong need for a standardization of dosimetry in radiobiology research, which will be most effective when the SOPs, education, and journal requirements are implemented in concert.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is a need for the radiobiology community to establish and follow dosimetry SOPs for cell culture and small and large animal studies, and for journals and conferences to provide continuing education in the form of tutorials on dosimetry, and to require adequate reporting of dosimetry.
the radiobiology community should adopt a standard set of dosimetry SOPs for cell culture and animal experiments and make them widely available.
we have identified a number of areas where improvement is possible and where we have made recommendations for improvement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for a set of dosimetry SOPs to be developed for radiobiology experiments, and a mechanism by which they can be widely disseminated.
the radiation physics and radiobiology communities need to work together to improve the quality of dosimetry in radiobiology research.
there is an urgent need to standardize dosimetry reporting for radiobiology experiments, and that this can be accomplished through the development and dissemination of SOPs.
